source_text: Ὅτι δὲ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν: Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τρία ἔλαβεν ἐν τῇ συνέσει δόγματα. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ: Καὶ διαθήσομαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὰ δικαιώματά μου. ἄρα οὖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντολὴ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ τρώγειν, Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν. τὸ οὖν χοιρίον πρὸς τοῦτο εἶπεν: οὐ κολληθήσῃ φησίν, ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινές εἰσιν ὅμοιοι χοίρων: τουτέστιν ὅταν σπαταλῶσιν, ἐπιλανθάνονται τοῦ κυρίου, ὅταν δὲ ὑστεροῦνται, ἐπιγινώσκουσιν τὸν κύριον, ὡς καὶ ὁ χοῖρος ὅταν τρώγει τὸν κύριον οὐκ οἶδεν, ὅταν δὲ πεινᾷ κραυγάζει, καὶ λαβὼν πάλιν σιωπᾷ. Οὐδὲ φάγῃ τὸν ἀετὸν οὐδὲ τὸν ὀξύπτερον οὐδὲ τὸν ἰκτῖνα οὐδὲ τὸν κόρακα: οὐ μή, φησίν, κολληθήσῃ οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες οὐκ οἴδασιν διὰ κόπου καὶ ἱδρῶτος πορίζειν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἁρπάζουσιν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἐν ἀνομίᾳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηροῦσιν ὡς ἐν ἀκεραιοσύνῃ περιπατοῦντες καὶ περιβλέπονται, τίνα ἐκδύσωσιν διὰ τὴν πλεονεξίαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὄρνεα ταῦτα μόνα ἑαυτοῖς οὐ προίζει τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἀργὰ καθήμενα ἐκζητεῖ, πῶς ἀλλοτρίας σάρκας καταφάγῃ, ὄντα λοιμὰ τῇ πονηρίᾳ αὐτῶν. Καὶ οὐ φάγῃ, φησίν, σμύραιναν οὐδὲ πολύποδα οὐδὲ σηπίαν: οὐ μή, φησίν, ὁμοιωθήσῃ κολλώμενος ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες εἰς τέλος εἰσὶν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ κεκριμένοι ἤδη τῷ θανάτῳ, ὡς καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἰχθύδια μόνα ἐπικατάρατα ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νήχεται, μὴ κολυμβῶντα ὡς τὰ λοιπά, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω τοῦ βυθοῦ κατοικεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν δασύποδα οὐ φάγῃ. πρὸς τί; οὐ μὴ γένῃ, φησίν, παιδοφθόρος οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις, ὅτι ὁ λαγωὸς κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν πλεονεκτεῖ τὴν ἀφόδευσιν: ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας. ἀλλὰ οὐδὲ τὴν ὕαιναν φάγῃ: οὐ μή, φησίν, γένῃ μοιχὸς οὐδὲ φθορεὺς οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις. πρὸς τί; ὅτι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο παρ ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσει τὴν φύσιν καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἄρρεν, ποτὲ δὲ θῆλυ γίνεται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γαλῆν ἐμίσησεν καλῶς. οὐ μή, φησίν, γενηθῇς τοιοῦτος, οἵους ἀκούομεν ἀνομίαν ποιοῦντας ἐν τῷ στόματι δἰ ἀκαθαρσίαν, οὐδὲ κολληθήσῃ ταῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι. τὸ γὰρ ζῷον τοῦτο τῷ στόματι κύει. περὶ μὲν τῶν βρωμάτων λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς τρία δόγματα οὕτως ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν: οἱ δὲ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς περὶ βρώσεως προσεδέξαντο. λαμβάνει δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν τριῶν δογμάτων γνῶσιν Δαυείδ καὶ λέγει: Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ ἰχθύες πορεύονται ἐν σκότει εἰς τὰ βάθη: καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη, καθὼς οἱ δοκοῦντες φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὡς ὁ χοῖρος, καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, καθὼς τὰ πετεινὰ καθήμενα εἰς ἁρπαγήν. ἔχετε τελείως καὶ περὶ τῆς βρώσεως. πάλιν λέγει Μωϋσῆς: Φάγεσθε πᾶν διχηλοῦν καὶ μαρυκώμενον. τί λέγει; ὅτι τὴν τροφὴν λαμβάνων οἶδεν τὸν τρέφοντα αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀναπαυόμενος εὐφραίνεσθαι δοκεῖ. καλῶς εἶπεν βλέπων τὴν ἐντολήν. τί οὖν λέγει; κολλᾶσθε μετὰ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν κύριον, μετὰ τῶν μελετώντων ὃ ἔλαβον διάσταλμα ῥήματος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, μετὰ τῶν λαλούντων τὰ διδαιώματα κυρίου καὶ τηρούντων, μετὰ τῶν εἰδότων, ὅτι ἡ μελέτη ἐστὶν ἔργον εὐφροσύνης, καὶ ἀναμαρυκωμένων τὸν λόγον κυρίου. τί δὲ τὸ διχηλοῦν; ὅτι ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ περιπατεῖ καὶ τὸν ἅγιον αἰῶνα ἐκδέχεται. βλέπετε, πῶς ἐνομοθέτησεν Μωϋσῆς καλῶς. ἀλλὰ πόθεν ἐκείνοις ταῦτα νοῆσαι ἢ συνιέναι; ἡμεῖς δὲ δικαίως νοήσαντες τὰς ἐντολὰς λαλοῦμεν, ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ κύριος. διὰ τοῦτο περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς καρδίας, ἵνα συνιῶμεν ταῦτα.
pass_a_gloss: For Moses said: You will not eat pig nor eagle nor sharp-sighted one nor crow nor all fish which does not have a scale in itself, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will make a covenant with this people my righteous deeds. Therefore it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore he said concerning the pig: You will not be joined, he says, to such people who are like pigs: that is when they squander they forget the Lord, when they are in need they recognize the Lord, just as the pig when it eats does not know the Lord, when it is hungry it cries out, and having eaten again it is silent. Nor will you eat the eagle nor the sharp-sighted one nor the fish nor the crow: Not, he says, will you be joined or likened to such people who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch as if walking in cunning and looking around, whom they might strip through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly they seek how they might devour the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness. And you will not eat, he says, the smyrnian nor the many-footed one nor the cuttlefish: Not, he says, will you be likened by joining with such people who are unrighteous and already judged to death, just as these little fish are alone cursed in the deep, not swimming as the others, but dwelling on the ground below the deep. But neither will you eat the hairy-footed one. Why? Not, he says, will you become a corrupter of children nor be likened to such, because the hare each year oversteps its burrow: for as many years as it lives, it has that many holes. But neither will you eat the hyena: Not, he says, will you become an adulterer nor a corrupter nor be likened to such. Why? Because this animal changes its nature each year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also he rightly hated the cat. Not, he says, will you become such, as we hear committing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor will you be joined to the unclean ones who commit lawlessness with the mouth. For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit: but they according to the desire of the flesh received it as concerning eating. And David receives knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the unrighteous, just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths: and in the way of sinners he did not stand, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and on the seat of the polluted he did not sit, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: Eat every split-footed and ruminating one. What does he say? That taking food he knows the one who nourishes him and resting on him seems to rejoice. He spoke well seeing the command. What then does he say? Be joined with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a distinction of word in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who ruminate on the word of the Lord. And what is the split-footed one? That the righteous one both walks in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where will they understand these things or comprehend? We, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore we have circumcised our ears and hearts, so that we might comprehend these things.
pass_b_english: Moses said, "You will not eat pig, eagle, vulture, crow, or any fish that lacks scales." He derived three spiritual principles from this command in his wisdom. In Deuteronomy he declares, "I will make my covenant with this people, my righteous acts" (Deuteronomy). Therefore the prohibition against eating is not a command of God about diet; Moses spoke by the Spirit. Concerning the pig he explains: "You must not associate with people who are like pigs. When they live in luxury they forget the Lord; when they are in need they acknowledge him. The pig behaves the same way: while it eats it does not know the Lord, but when it is hungry it cries out, and after eating it falls silent again." He also forbids the eagle, the vulture, the kite, and the crow: "You must not associate or become like those who do not know how to provide their own food by labor and sweat. Instead they seize what belongs to others through lawlessness. They watch with cunning, looking around to see whom they can strip through greed, all the while pretending to walk in innocence. These birds do not provide for themselves; they sit idle and wait to devour the flesh of others, corrupted by their own wickedness." He further says, "You will not eat the sea-mouse, the octopus, or the cuttlefish. You must not become like those who join themselves to such people—people who are utterly ungodly and already condemned to death. These creatures are cursed in the depths; they do not swim like other fish but dwell on the bottom of the sea." You must not eat the hare either. Why? "So that you will not become a corrupter of children or resemble such people. The hare adds a new passage each year; it has as many burrows as the years it lives." You must not eat the hyena either: "So that you will not become an adulterer or a corrupter or resemble them. This animal changes its nature every year, becoming male one year and female the next." He also rightly detested the weasel: "You must not become like those we hear of who commit lawlessness with their mouths through uncleanness, nor associate with the unclean women who commit lawlessness with their mouths. This animal conceives through its mouth." Regarding food, then, Moses received three doctrines and spoke them by the Spirit, but people received them according to fleshly desire as mere dietary rules. David received understanding of the same three doctrines and said, "Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, just as fish swim in darkness toward the depths; who does not stand in the way of sinners, just as those who appear to fear the Lord sin like the pig; and who does not sit in the seat of scoffers, just as birds sit waiting to plunder" (Psalm 1:1). You now have the complete interpretation of the food laws. Moses says again, "Eat every animal that has a split hoof and chews the cud." What does he mean? When it takes food it knows the one who feeds it, and resting on him it seems to rejoice. He spoke well because he saw the true intent of the command. So what is he saying? "Associate with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on the commandment they have received in their hearts, with those who speak the Lord's teachings and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who chew over the word of the Lord." What does "split hoof" signify? That the righteous person walks in this world and also awaits the holy age to come. See how well Moses legislated. But how could they understand or comprehend these things? We, having rightly understood the commandments, speak as the Lord willed. That is why we have circumcised our ears and hearts, so that we might comprehend these things.

review.notes: Pass B fails on several translation accuracy points compared to the Locked Greek: 1. 'ἰκτῖνα' is translated as 'kite' in Pass B, whereas Pass A correctly identifies it as 'the fish' (though 'kite' is a bird, the Greek context here refers to fish/sea creatures in the list). 2. 'σμύραιναν' is translated as 'sea-mouse' in Pass B, which is a valid rendering, but 'σμήραιναν' (likely OCR/text error for smyrainan) is rendered as 'smyrnian' in Pass A; however, Pass B's 'octopus' for 'πολύποδα' is a reasonable gloss, but the mismatch in the bird list (eagle, vulture, kite, crow) vs Greek (ἀετὸν, ὀξύπτερον, ἰκτῖνα, κόρακα) is problematic if ἰκτῖνα is treated as a bird 'kite' while the Greek list is clearly part of the dietary prohibitions including fish. 3. 'γαλῆν' is translated as 'weasel' in Pass B, but the Greek 'γαλῆν' and Pass A's 'cat' are the standard translations; 'weasel' is a departure. 4. 'καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν' is translated as 'on the seat of scoffers' in Pass B, but the Greek 'λοιμῶν' means 'the polluted/diseased/pestilential ones', not 'scoffers' (which would be 'ἐμπείδων' or similar). Pass B's 'scoffers' changes the doctrine from being associated with the unclean/diseased to being associated with the proud/mocking.
reasons: Pass B translates 'λοιμῶν' as 'scoffers', which contradicts the Greek 'λοιμῶν' (the polluted/diseased/pestilential ones) and changes the doctrinal meaning. Pass B translates 'γαλῆν' as 'weasel' instead of 'cat'. Pass B translates 'ἰκτῖνα' as 'kite' (a bird) in a list that the Greek structure treats as part of the fish/sea creature prohibitions (though ἰκτῖνα can be a bird, the context of the surrounding fish/sea creatures and Pass A's 'fish' suggests a specific reading).

review.notes: greek/barnabas.xml:1: "Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ"; Pass A: "You will not eat pig nor eagle nor sharp-sighted one nor crow nor all fish which does not have a scale in itself"; Pass B: "You will not eat pig, eagle, vulture, crow, or any fish that lacks scales"
